security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU does not define SMSTATEEN0_ACLIC at bit 53 in cpu_bits.h, does not include it in write_mstateen0's wr_mask, and has no smstateen_acc_ok check gating S-mode access to acliciprio/aclicsourcecfg CSRs. Consequently: (1) mstateen0 bit 53 is always read-as-zero/write-ignored (WARL-zero), so M-mode cannot grant S-mode access to ACLIC CSRs; (2) if ACLIC CSRs are emulated, S-mode access is either unconditionally allowed (missing trap) or unconditionally denied (breaking M-mode delegation).
security_spec.summary: Missing mstateen0 bit 53 (ACLIC) definition and access gating in QEMU emulation undermines Smstateen-based isolation of ACLIC CSRs from S-mode

findings.finding: SMSTATEEN0_ACLIC bit 53 is not defined in cpu_bits.h. The ACLIC fast-interrupt spec (aclic.adoc:656) requires bit 53 of mstateen0 to control S-mode access to acliciprio/aclicsourcecfg CSRs when both Smstateen and ACLIC extensions are implemented. Currently QEMU does not emulate ACLIC CSRs, so bit 53 is implicitly read-as-zero/write-ignored (correct for no-ACLIC). However, if ACLIC CSR support is added in the future without also adding this bit, S-mode access to ACLIC CSRs would either be unconditionally allowed (privilege escape) or unconditionally denied (breaking M-mode delegation).
findings.snippet:
#define SMSTATEEN0_CS       (1ULL << 0)
#define SMSTATEEN0_FCSR     (1ULL << 1)
#define SMSTATEEN0_JVT      (1ULL << 2)
#define SMSTATEEN0_CTR      (1ULL << 54)
#define SMSTATEEN0_P1P13    (1ULL << 56)
...no SMSTATEEN0_ACLIC at bit 53...

spec_citations.excerpt: Additional control is provided for the newly added registers acliciprio[k] and aclicsourcecfg[k]. If the Smstateen extension is implemented, then the bit 53 (ACLIC) in mstateen0 is implemented. If bit 53 (ACLIC) of a controlling mstateen0 CSR is zero, then access to the new CSRs (acliciprio[k], aclicsourcecfg[k]) by S-mode or a lower-privilege mode results in an illegal instruction exception.

findings.finding: write_mstateen0's wr_mask does not include SMSTATEEN0_ACLIC (bit 53). This is consistent with the missing define in cpu_bits.h. If ACLIC CSRs are later added, this function would fail to gate bit 53 writability, meaning even if bit 53 were defined, M-mode writes to bit 53 would be silently ignored (WARL-zero). Conditional inclusion (e.g., based on a future ext_smaclic property) would be needed, following the existing pattern for ext_ssaia gating SMSTATEEN0_AIA/IMSIC.

spec_citations.excerpt: If the Smstateen extension is implemented, then the bit 53 (ACLIC) in mstateen0 is implemented. If bit 53 (ACLIC) of a controlling mstateen0 CSR is zero, then access to the new CSRs (acliciprio[k], aclicsourcecfg[k]) by S-mode or a lower-privilege mode results in an illegal instruction exception.

findings.finding: smstateen_acc_ok() is a generic gate function that checks env->mstateen[index] & bit. It correctly handles M-mode bypass, virt/hypervisor layering, and user-mode sstateen checks. No functional issue with this function itself — it would work correctly if SMSTATEEN0_ACLIC were defined and passed as the bit argument. The gap is that no code path calls smstateen_acc_ok(env, 0, SMSTATEEN0_ACLIC) for ACLIC CSR access gating.

write_mstateen0h's wr_mask (high 32-bit half of mstateen0) also lacks SMSTATEEN0_ACLIC at bit 53. Since bit 53 is in the upper 32 bits (53 > 31), the high-half CSR write path must also include this bit. Currently missing, consistent with the missing define in cpu_bits.h.

spec_citations.excerpt: If the Smstateen extension is implemented, then the bit 53 (ACLIC) in mstateen0 is implemented.

findings.finding: QEMU currently does not implement any ACLIC CSRs (acliciprio, aclicsourcecfg, spistatus, sithreshold, sivt, seivt). Absent ACLIC emulation, the base Smstateen spec (smstateen.adoc line 138-140) is satisfied: bits controlling unimplemented state must be read-only zero, and bit 53 falls within the WPRI range (bits 3-53) per the base mstateen0 wavedrom layout. The current behavior — where bit 53 is implicitly ROZ because no write mask includes it — is technically spec-compliant for a non-ACLIC hart.

spec_citations.excerpt: Bits in any stateen CSR that are defined to control state that a hart doesn't implement are read-only zeros for that hart. Likewise, all reserved bits not yet given a defined meaning are also read-only zeros.
